<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
\label{def:action-sufficient-target}
A variable $Z_t^\star\in\mathcal Z_t$ is an
\emph{action-sufficient coordination target} for receiver $j$ if
$A_t^{j,\star}\perp S_t^i \mid (X_t^j,Z_t^\star)$, where
$A_t^{j,\star}$ is the optimal next action.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:communication-tax}
For any deployed protocol $\rho$ and step loss $\ell$,
\begin{equation}
U_{\rho,\ell}(M_t;Z_t^\star)
=
R_\rho(0)-R_\rho(1)
=
A_{C,\ell}^\star(M_t;Z_t^\star)-\tau_{\rho,\ell}(M_t).
\label{eq:tax-identity}
\end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:compression-dominance}
Under log-loss, if $M_t=f(C_t)$, then
\begin{equation}
\Delta U_{\rm cmp-raw}
=
\Delta\tau_{\rm raw\to cmp}
-
\mathcal I_{\rm omit}
-
\Lambda_C(M_t\!\to\!C_t).
\label{eq:cmp-vs-raw-gap}
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
\label{def:alpha-proper}
For $0<\alpha<1$, $M_t=T(C_t)$ is an
\emph{$\alpha$-proper Bayes-sufficient compression} of $C_t$ for
target $Z_t^\star$ and receiver view $X_t^j$ if
(i) $I(Z_t^\star;C_t\mid X_t^j,M_t)=0$ and
(ii) $H(M_t)\le \alpha H(C_t)$.
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:sufficiency-not-enough}
For any $0<\alpha<1$ and $\varepsilon>0$, there exist a task, an
$\alpha$-proper Bayes-sufficient compression
(Definition~\ref{def:alpha-proper}), and a representation-sensitive
receiver class on which the raw context attains zero error, while the
compressed message incurs an error of at least $1/2-\varepsilon$.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:bottleneck-chain}
For any bottleneck-factorized receiver,
\begin{equation}
L_{\rm total}=L_{\rm ext}+L_{\rm abs}+L_{\rm close}.
\label{eq:loss-decomp-identity}
\end{equation}
Each term is nonnegative. The terms correspond respectively to
externalization, absorption, and action closure.
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:replay-isolation}
For two receivers evaluated on the same local input, broader context,
and the same message generated by a fixed sender and held fixed during replay, the sender-side externalization term cancels. The paired
difference, therefore, depends only on receiver-side absorption and
action-closure terms.
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- definition-3: body_md -->
\label{def:burden-family}
A receiver family $\{R_b:b\in\mathcal B\}$ is
\emph{burden-indexed} if each receiver's local insufficiency is
summarized by a scalar burden $b$, such as
$H(Z_t^\star\mid X_t^{R_b})$ or an empirical receiver-only proxy.
<!-- end definition-3 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{prop:alignment-threshold}
For any step loss $\ell$ and fixed executor $R$,
\[
U_{s',R,\ell}-U_{s,R,\ell}
=
\Delta A_{R,\ell}(s,s')-\Delta\tau_{R,\ell}(s,s').
\]
For a burden-indexed family, let $\Psi_{s,s'}(b)$ be this net value
at burden $b$. If $\Psi_{s,s'}$ is continuous and single-crossing,
with negative value at low burden and positive value at high burden,
then there is a unique threshold $b^\star$ at which the stronger
upstream agent changes from harmful to helpful.
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
\label{prop:conditional-propagation}
Suppose two trajectories share the same $(k_t,q_t,\lambda_t)$
sequence and differ only through an initial residual gap $\Delta_t$.
If $D_u>q_u$ and $\widetilde D_u>q_u$ for all
$u=t,\ldots,t+h-1$, then
\[
\Delta_{t+h}
=
\Bigl(\prod_{u=t}^{t+h-1}\lambda_u\Bigr)\Delta_t.
\]
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:gamma-nonnegative}
For any conditioning variable $Y$ and any receiver class $\Phi_C$ of predictive distributions under log-loss,
\[
\Gamma_C(Y)
:=
\mathcal R_{C,\log}^\star(Z_t^\star\mid Y)
-
H(Z_t^\star\mid Y)
\ge 0.
\]
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
For any admissible predictor $q_\phi(\cdot\mid Y)$,
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{E}[-\log q_\phi(Z_t^\star\mid Y)]
&=
\mathbb{E}[-\log p(Z_t^\star\mid Y)]
+
\mathbb{E}\!\left[
\log \frac{p(Z_t^\star\mid Y)}{q_\phi(Z_t^\star\mid Y)}
\right] \\
&=
H(Z_t^\star\mid Y)
+
\mathbb{E}\!\left[
\mathrm{KL}\bigl(p(\cdot\mid Y)\,\|\,q_\phi(\cdot\mid Y)\bigr)
\right]\\
&\ge
H(Z_t^\star\mid Y).
\end{align*}
Taking the infimum over $\phi\in\Phi_C$ gives the claim.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
By definition,
\[
U_{\rho,\ell}(M_t;Z_t^\star)=R_\rho(0)-R_\rho(1).
\]
Add and subtract $R_C^\star(0)$ and $R_C^\star(1)$:
\begin{align*}
U_{\rho,\ell}(M_t;Z_t^\star)
&=
R_\rho(0)-R_\rho(1)
+R_C^\star(0)-R_C^\star(0)
+R_C^\star(1)-R_C^\star(1)\\
&=
\bigl(R_C^\star(0)-R_C^\star(1)\bigr)
-
\Bigl[
\bigl(R_\rho(1)-R_C^\star(1)\bigr)
-
\bigl(R_\rho(0)-R_C^\star(0)\bigr)
\Bigr].
\end{align*}
The first bracket is $A_{C,\ell}^\star(M_t;Z_t^\star)$ and the second bracket is $\tau_{\rho,\ell}(M_t)$.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
By Lemma~\ref{lem:gamma-nonnegative} and the definition of $\Gamma_C$,
\[
\mathcal R_{C,\log}^\star(Z_t^\star\mid Y)
=
H(Z_t^\star\mid Y)+\Gamma_C(Y)
\]
for every conditioning variable $Y$ considered below.

Apply this identity to $Y=X_t^j$ and $Y=(X_t^j,M_t)$:
\begin{align*}
A_{C,\log}^\star(M_t;Z_t^\star)
&=
\mathcal R_{C,\log}^\star(Z_t^\star\mid X_t^j)
-
\mathcal R_{C,\log}^\star(Z_t^\star\mid X_t^j,M_t)\\
&=
H(Z_t^\star\mid X_t^j)-H(Z_t^\star\mid X_t^j,M_t)
+
\Gamma_C(X_t^j)-\Gamma_C(X_t^j,M_t)\\
&=
I(Z_t^\star;M_t\mid X_t^j)
+
\Gamma_C(X_t^j)-\Gamma_C(X_t^j,M_t).
\end{align*}

Similarly, conditioning on raw context gives
\[
A_{C,\log}^\star(C_t;Z_t^\star)
=
I(Z_t^\star;C_t\mid X_t^j)
+
\Gamma_C(X_t^j)-\Gamma_C(X_t^j,C_t).
\]
Subtracting the compressed-message gain from the raw-context gain yields
\begin{align*}
A_{C,\log}^\star(C_t;Z_t^\star)
-
A_{C,\log}^\star(M_t;Z_t^\star)
&=
I(Z_t^\star;C_t\mid X_t^j)
-
I(Z_t^\star;M_t\mid X_t^j)\\
&\quad+
\Gamma_C(X_t^j,M_t)-\Gamma_C(X_t^j,C_t).
\end{align*}
Because $M_t=f(C_t)$ is deterministic, the conditional chain rule gives
\[
I(Z_t^\star;C_t\mid X_t^j)
=
I(Z_t^\star;M_t\mid X_t^j)
+
I(Z_t^\star;C_t\mid X_t^j,M_t).
\]
Therefore
\[
A_{C,\log}^\star(C_t;Z_t^\star)
-
A_{C,\log}^\star(M_t;Z_t^\star)
=
I(Z_t^\star;C_t\mid X_t^j,M_t)
+
\Lambda_C(M_t\!\to\!C_t),
\]
where
\[
\Lambda_C(M_t\!\to\!C_t)
:=
\Gamma_C(X_t^j,M_t)-\Gamma_C(X_t^j,C_t).
\]

Apply Proposition~\ref{thm:communication-tax} to the compressed protocol and to the raw-context protocol:
\[
U_{\rho_{\rm cmp},\log}(M_t;Z_t^\star)
=
A_{C,\log}^\star(M_t;Z_t^\star)
-
\tau_{\rho_{\rm cmp},\log}(M_t),
\]
\[
U_{\rho_{\rm raw},\log}(C_t;Z_t^\star)
=
A_{C,\log}^\star(C_t;Z_t^\star)
-
\tau_{\rho_{\rm raw},\log}(C_t).
\]
Subtracting the second identity from the first gives
\begin{align*}
\Delta U_{\rm cmp-raw}
&=
U_{\rho_{\rm cmp},\log}(M_t;Z_t^\star)
-
U_{\rho_{\rm raw},\log}(C_t;Z_t^\star)\\
&=
\bigl(A_{C,\log}^\star(M_t;Z_t^\star)
-
A_{C,\log}^\star(C_t;Z_t^\star)\bigr)
+
\bigl(\tau_{\rho_{\rm raw},\log}(C_t)-\tau_{\rho_{\rm cmp},\log}(M_t)\bigr)\\
&=
\Delta\tau_{\rm raw\to cmp}
-
I(Z_t^\star;C_t\mid X_t^j,M_t)
-
\Lambda_C(M_t\!\to\!C_t),
\end{align*}
which is Eq.~\eqref{eq:cmp-vs-raw-gap}.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
\label{prop:receiver-class-certificate}
Under log-loss, if $M_t=f(C_t)$, then
\[
B_C(M_t,C_t)
=
I(Z_t^\star;C_t\mid X_t^j,M_t)
+
\Lambda_C(M_t\!\to\!C_t).
\]
Consequently,
\[
\Delta U_{\rm cmp-raw}
=
\Delta\tau_{\rm raw\to cmp}
-
B_C(M_t,C_t).
\]
Thus, compressed communication dominates raw-context execution exactly when the tax saved by compression exceeds the bounded-receiver representation gap.
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
By the log-loss slack identity,
\begin{align*}
B_C(M_t,C_t)
&=
\Bigl[
H(Z_t^\star\mid X_t^j,M_t)+\Gamma_C(X_t^j,M_t)
\Bigr]\\
&\quad-
\Bigl[
H(Z_t^\star\mid X_t^j,C_t)+\Gamma_C(X_t^j,C_t)
\Bigr]\\
&=
H(Z_t^\star\mid X_t^j,M_t)
-
H(Z_t^\star\mid X_t^j,C_t)
+
\Lambda_C(M_t\!\to\!C_t).
\end{align*}
Because $M_t=f(C_t)$, the entropy difference equals
\[
H(Z_t^\star\mid X_t^j,M_t)
-
H(Z_t^\star\mid X_t^j,C_t)
=
I(Z_t^\star;C_t\mid X_t^j,M_t).
\]
This proves the first identity. The second identity follows by substituting this expression into Eq.~\eqref{eq:cmp-vs-raw-gap}.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:compatibility}
If $B_C(M_t,C_t)\le \kappa_t$, then compressed communication dominates raw-context execution whenever
\[
\Delta\tau_{\rm raw\to cmp}>\kappa_t.
\]
Equivalently, if $\Lambda_C(M_t\!\to\!C_t)\le \bar\kappa_t$, then compression dominates whenever
\[
\Delta\tau_{\rm raw\to cmp}>
I(Z_t^\star;C_t\mid X_t^j,M_t)+\bar\kappa_t.
\]
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
The first statement is immediate from Proposition~\ref{prop:receiver-class-certificate}. The second follows by substituting
\[
B_C(M_t,C_t)
=
I(Z_t^\star;C_t\mid X_t^j,M_t)
+
\Lambda_C(M_t\!\to\!C_t).
\]
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:alternating-threshold}
Let $M$ be uniform on $\{0,1,\ldots,2m-1\}$, and let the binary label alternate on the ordered message axis:
\[
Z(M)=
\begin{cases}
0, & M \text{ even},\\
1, & M \text{ odd}.
\end{cases}
\]
For the threshold class
\[
\Phi_{\rm thr}
=
\{h_\theta(M)=\mathbf 1\{M\ge \theta\}:\theta\in\mathbb R\},
\]
the optimal $0/1$ error is at least $(m-1)/(2m)$.
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
Any threshold is equivalent to choosing a cut index $k\in\{0,1,\ldots,2m\}$, predicting $0$ on the first $k$ ordered message values and $1$ on the remaining $2m-k$ values. If $k=2r$ is even, the first segment contains $r$ positive labels and the second segment contains $m-r$ negative labels, so the threshold makes $m$ mistakes. If $k=2r+1$ is odd, the first segment contains $r$ positive labels and the second segment contains $m-r-1$ negative labels, so it makes $m-1$ mistakes. The boundary cases $k=0$ and $k=2m$ each make $m$ mistakes. Therefore, each threshold incurs at least $m-1$ mistakes among the $2m$ equiprobable states.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
Fix any compression ratio $\alpha\in(0,1)$ and any $\varepsilon>0$. Choose $m\ge 2$ large enough that
\[
\frac{m-1}{2m}\ge \frac12-\varepsilon.
\]
Let
\[
Y\sim \mathrm{Unif}\{0,1,\ldots,2m-1\},
\qquad
U\sim \mathrm{Unif}\{1,\ldots,K\},
\]
independently, and define the raw context
\[
C=(Y,U).
\]
The nuisance coordinate $U$ carries no target information but contributes to raw-context size. Let
\[
Z:=\mathbf 1\{Y\ge m\}.
\]

The bounded receiver class is representation-sensitive. It thresholds the visible scalar coordinate delivered by the protocol. In the raw context, the visible coordinate is the natural coordinate $Y$; on a compressed scalar message, the visible coordinate is the message value. Formally, define
\[
\operatorname{coord}(Y,U)=Y,
\qquad
\operatorname{coord}(M)=M,
\]
and let
\[
\Phi_{\rm thr}
=
\left\{
h_\theta(v)=\mathbf 1\{\operatorname{coord}(v)\ge \theta\}:\theta\in\mathbb R
\right\}.
\]
Thus, the raw context is decoded by thresholding $Y$, whereas the compressed message is decoded by thresholding the delivered surface value $M$.

On raw context, the threshold $\theta^\star=m-\frac12$ achieves zero error:
\[
h_{\theta^\star}(Y,U)=\mathbf 1\{Y\ge m\}=Z.
\]
Therefore
\[
\mathcal R_{\Phi_{\rm thr},0/1}^\star(Z\mid C)=0.
\]

Now define a recoding $f:\{0,\ldots,2m-1\}\to\{0,\ldots,2m-1\}$ by
\[
f(i)=2i,\qquad i=0,\ldots,m-1,
\]
and
\[
f(m+i)=2i+1,\qquad i=0,\ldots,m-1.
\]
The compressed message drops the nuisance coordinate and sends
\[
M:=T(C):=f(Y).
\]

Because $f$ is a bijection on $Y$, the value of $Y$ is a deterministic function of $M$. Since $Z$ is a deterministic function of $Y$, we have
\[
I(Z;C\mid M)=0.
\]
Thus $M$ is Bayes-sufficient.

The message is also properly compressed. Since $f$ is bijective on $Y$,
\[
H(M)=H(Y)=\log(2m).
\]
Because $Y$ and $U$ are independent,
\[
H(C)=H(Y,U)=\log(2m)+\log K.
\]
Choose
\[
K\ge \left\lceil (2m)^{(1-\alpha)/\alpha}\right\rceil.
\]
Then
\[
H(M)
=
\log(2m)
\le
\alpha\bigl(\log(2m)+\log K\bigr)
=
\alpha H(C).
\]
Thus $M$ is an $\alpha$-proper Bayes-sufficient compression.

It remains to be shown that the error on the compressed representation is lower-bounded. Under the ordered message values $M=0,1,\ldots,2m-1$, labels alternate:
\[
Z=0,1,0,1,\ldots,0,1.
\]
The negative states $Y=0,\ldots,m-1$ map to even message values, while the positive states $Y=m,\ldots,2m-1$ map to odd message values. By Lemma~\ref{lem:alternating-threshold},
\[
\mathcal R_{\Phi_{\rm thr},0/1}^\star(Z\mid M)
\ge
\frac{m-1}{2m}
\ge
\frac12-\varepsilon.
\]
Thus, the raw context is decoded perfectly by the bounded receiver class, while an $\alpha$-proper Bayes-sufficient compressed message has error arbitrarily close to balanced binary chance error.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- definition-4: body_md -->
\label{def:receiver-compatible-sufficient}
A Bayes-sufficient compression $M_t=f(C_t)$ is $\kappa$-receiver-compatible for class $\Phi_C$ if
\[
B_C(M_t,C_t)
=
\mathcal R^\star_{C,\log}(Z_t^\star\mid X_t^j,M_t)
-
\mathcal R^\star_{C,\log}(Z_t^\star\mid X_t^j,C_t)
\le \kappa.
\]
<!-- end definition-4 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
\label{cor:receiver-compatible-sufficiency}
If $M_t=f(C_t)$ is Bayes-sufficient for $Z_t^\star$ given $X_t^j$, then
\[
I(Z_t^\star;C_t\mid X_t^j,M_t)=0
\]
and
\[
\Delta U_{\rm cmp-raw}
=
\Delta\tau_{\rm raw\to cmp}
-
\Lambda_C(M_t\!\to\!C_t).
\]
More generally, if $M_t$ is $\kappa$-receiver-compatible, compressed communication dominates raw context whenever
\[
\Delta\tau_{\rm raw\to cmp}>\kappa.
\]
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
Bayes sufficiency sets the omitted-information term in Eq.~\eqref{eq:cmp-vs-raw-gap} to zero, leaving only the decoder-mismatch term. The general statement follows from Proposition~\ref{prop:receiver-class-certificate}: if $B_C(M_t,C_t)\le\kappa$, then
\[
\Delta U_{\rm cmp-raw}
=
\Delta\tau_{\rm raw\to cmp}
-
B_C(M_t,C_t)
\ge
\Delta\tau_{\rm raw\to cmp}-\kappa.
\]
Thus, compression beats raw context whenever the saved tax exceeds the receiver-class representation gap.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
The useful target is not Bayes sufficiency alone, but receiver-compatible sufficiency: the message should preserve the action-sufficient target, reduce protocol tax, and present the target in a surface form usable by the bounded receiver.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
Define the adjacent drops
\[
L_{\rm ext}
:=
I(Z_t^\star;C_t\mid X_t^j)-I(Z_t^\star;M_t\mid X_t^j),
\]
\[
L_{\rm abs}
:=
I(Z_t^\star;M_t\mid X_t^j)-I(Z_t^\star;\widehat Z_t\mid X_t^j),
\]
and
\[
L_{\rm close}
:=
I(Z_t^\star;\widehat Z_t\mid X_t^j)-I(Z_t^\star;A_t^j\mid X_t^j).
\]
By the data-processing inequality applied along
\[
Z_t^\star \to C_t \to M_t \to \widehat Z_t \to A_t^j
\]
conditional on $X_t^j$, each adjacent drop is nonnegative. Summing the adjacent drops gives the telescoping identity
\[
I(Z_t^\star;C_t\mid X_t^j)-I(Z_t^\star;A_t^j\mid X_t^j)
=
L_{\rm ext}+L_{\rm abs}+L_{\rm close}.
\]
The left-hand side is $L_{\rm total}$.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
For a receiver $r$ evaluated on the fixed triple $(X_t,C_t,M_t)$, Theorem~\ref{thm:bottleneck-chain} gives
\[
I(Z_t^\star;A_t^{r}\mid X_t)
=
I(Z_t^\star;M_t\mid X_t)
-
L_{\rm abs}^{r}
-
L_{\rm close}^{r}.
\]
The term $I(Z_t^\star;M_t\mid X_t)$ is shared by all receivers in a fixed-message replay setting. Therefore, for two receivers $r,r'$,
\begin{align*}
I(Z_t^\star;A_t^{r}\mid X_t)
-
I(Z_t^\star;A_t^{r'}\mid X_t)
&=
\bigl(L_{\rm abs}^{r'}+L_{\rm close}^{r'}\bigr)
-
\bigl(L_{\rm abs}^{r}+L_{\rm close}^{r}\bigr).
\end{align*}
Thus, sender-side externalization cancels in the paired comparison, leaving receiver-side absorption and action closure.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
For a fixed executor $R$, apply Proposition~\ref{thm:communication-tax} to the sender $s$ and to the stronger sender $s'$:
\[
U_{s,R,\ell}
=
A_{R,\ell}^\star(M_t^{s};Z_t^\star)
-
\tau_{s,R,\ell}(M_t^{s}),
\]
\[
U_{s',R,\ell}
=
A_{R,\ell}^\star(M_t^{s'};Z_t^\star)
-
\tau_{s',R,\ell}(M_t^{s'}).
\]
Subtracting gives
\[
U_{s',R,\ell}-U_{s,R,\ell}
=
\Delta A_{R,\ell}(s,s')-\Delta\tau_{R,\ell}(s,s').
\]

Now let $\{R_b:b\in\mathcal B\}$ be a burden-indexed receiver family and define
\[
\Psi_{s,s'}(b)
:=
U_{s',R_b,\ell}-U_{s,R_b,\ell}.
\]
If $\Psi_{s,s'}$ is continuous and strictly single-crossing, its sign changes at most once. If it is negative at low burden and positive at high burden, the intermediate value theorem gives a crossing $b^\star$ with $\Psi_{s,s'}(b^\star)=0$, and strict single-crossing makes this crossing unique since the stronger sender helps exactly when $\Psi_{s,s'}(b)>0$, it helps exactly on the high-burden side of $b^\star$.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
The residual dynamics are
\[
D_{u+1}=k_u+\lambda_u[D_u-q_u]_+,
\qquad
\widetilde D_{u+1}=k_u+\lambda_u[\widetilde D_u-q_u]_+.
\]
If $D_u>q_u$ and $\widetilde D_u>q_u$, then clipping is inactive:
\[
[D_u-q_u]_+=D_u-q_u,
\qquad
[\widetilde D_u-q_u]_+=\widetilde D_u-q_u.
\]
Therefore
\[
\Delta_{u+1}
=
\widetilde D_{u+1}-D_{u+1}
=
\lambda_u(\widetilde D_u-D_u)
=
\lambda_u\Delta_u.
\]
Iterating for $u=t,\ldots,t+h-1$ gives
\[
\Delta_{t+h}
=
\left(\prod_{u=t}^{t+h-1}\lambda_u\right)\Delta_t.
\]
If clipping becomes active for either trajectory, the difference is no longer propagated linearly; this is the resynchronization regime, as represented by the clipped residual model. For vector-valued residuals, the same argument applies componentwise when the carry condition holds componentwise.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- proposition-5: body_md -->
\label{prop:plugin-selector-regret}
Suppose that for every $\alpha\in\mathcal A_t$,
\[
|\widehat J_t(\alpha)-J_t(\alpha)|\le \epsilon.
\]
Then the one-step value regret of the deployed selector satisfies
\[
J_t(\alpha_t^\star)-J_t(\widehat\alpha_t)\le 2\epsilon.
\]
<!-- end proposition-5 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
By optimality of $\widehat\alpha_t$ under $\widehat J_t$,
\[
\widehat J_t(\widehat\alpha_t)\ge \widehat J_t(\alpha_t^\star).
\]
Using the uniform error bound twice,
\[
J_t(\alpha_t^\star)
\le
\widehat J_t(\alpha_t^\star)+\epsilon
\le
\widehat J_t(\widehat\alpha_t)+\epsilon
\le
J_t(\widehat\alpha_t)+2\epsilon.
\]
Rearranging gives the claim.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- corollary-3: body_md -->
\label{cor:termwise-selector-regret}
Suppose the deployed score uses
\[
\widehat J_t(\alpha)
=
\widehat A_t(\alpha)
-
\widehat\tau_t(\alpha)
-
\eta_c \widehat c(\alpha)
-
\eta_r \widehat r_t(\alpha),
\]
and for every $\alpha\in\mathcal A_t$,
\[
|\widehat A_t(\alpha)-A_t(\alpha)|\le \epsilon_A,\qquad
|\widehat\tau_t(\alpha)-\tau_t(\alpha)|\le \epsilon_\tau,
\]
\[
|\widehat c(\alpha)-c(\alpha)|\le \epsilon_c,\qquad
|\widehat r_t(\alpha)-r_t(\alpha)|\le \epsilon_r.
\]
Then
\[
J_t(\alpha_t^\star)-J_t(\widehat\alpha_t)
\le
2\bigl(\epsilon_A+\epsilon_\tau+\eta_c\epsilon_c+\eta_r\epsilon_r\bigr).
\]
<!-- end corollary-3 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
The termwise bounds imply
\[
|\widehat J_t(\alpha)-J_t(\alpha)|
\le
\epsilon_A+\epsilon_\tau+\eta_c\epsilon_c+\eta_r\epsilon_r
\]
uniformly over $\alpha$. Apply Proposition~\ref{prop:plugin-selector-regret}.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- proposition-6: body_md -->
\label{prop:factorized-target}
Suppose $Z_t^\star=(Z_t^{\rm art},Z_t^{\rm act})$, the loss decomposes additively across the two factors, and the admissible receiver class factorizes into independent artifact and action predictors. Then the class-optimal risk and the receiver-relative gain decompose into artifact and action components.
<!-- end proposition-6 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
Under additive loss and a product receiver class, optimizing the joint predictor separates into optimizing the artifact predictor and the action predictor. The class-optimal joint risk is therefore the sum of the two class-optimal factor risks. Subtracting the no-message and message-conditioned versions gives the same additive decomposition for the receiver-relative gain.
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- proposition-7: body_md -->
\label{prop:variational-benefit}
Under the zero-slack specialization,
\[
A_{C,\log}^\star(M_t;Z_t^\star)
=
I(M_t;Z_t^\star\mid X_t^j).
\]
Hence, for any uniformly bounded critic class $\mathcal T$,
\[
A_{\mathcal T}(M_t;Z_t^\star\mid X_t^j)
:=
\sup_{T\in\mathcal T}
\left\{
\mathbb{E}_{p(X,M,Z)}[T]
-
\log
\mathbb{E}_{p(X)p(M\mid X)p(Z\mid X)}[e^T]
\right\}
\le
A_{C,\log}^\star(M_t;Z_t^\star).
\]
Consequently,
\[
\tau_{\rho,\log}(M_t)
\ge
A_{\mathcal T}(M_t;Z_t^\star\mid X_t^j)
-
U_{\rho,\log}(M_t;Z_t^\star).
\]
<!-- end proposition-7 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
Under zero slack, the log-loss receiver-relative gain equals conditional mutual information:
\[
A_{C,\log}^\star(M_t;Z_t^\star)
=
I(M_t;Z_t^\star\mid X_t^j).
\]
Conditional mutual information is the KL divergence
\[
I(M_t;Z_t^\star\mid X_t^j)
=
\mathrm{KL}\!\left(
p(X_t^j,M_t,Z_t^\star)
\;\middle\|\;
p(X_t^j)p(M_t\mid X_t^j)p(Z_t^\star\mid X_t^j)
\right).
\]
The Donsker--Varadhan representation of KL, restricted to the uniformly bounded critic class $\mathcal T$, gives the stated lower bound. The tax certificate follows by rearranging Proposition~\ref{thm:communication-tax}:
\[
\tau_{\rho,\log}(M_t)
=
A_{C,\log}^\star(M_t;Z_t^\star)
-
U_{\rho,\log}(M_t;Z_t^\star).
\]
<!-- end proof-16 -->

A \textcolor{orange}{[No]}{} or \textcolor{gray}{[N/A]}{} answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers.
